items.title: Exact real scalar free model
items.design_state: Exact real scalar specialization with explicit shell, Fock domain and vacuum-subtracted Hamiltonian; conditional on the QFT-F01 physical adoption.
items.physical_scope: One real scalar species in four-dimensional flat Minkowski spacetime, with the adopted bosonic Fock representation, inverse-length parameter μ≥0, and exact vacuum-subtracted Hamiltonian ℏc dΓs(ωμ). This definition supplies no interacting term, regulator, point-field product, or empirical universality claim.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], as in the inspected Fock
construction.

Select the real-scalar branch of the QFT-F01 physical adoption
[[post-qft-free-field-model]]: one real spin-zero species with bosonic
statistics and the zero-particle vacuum. For a smooth real classical field
$\phi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb R$ of canonical length degree $-1$,
that postulate adopts the local action density represented by
$$\frac{S_\phi}{\hbar}=-\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^4} \left(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi_{\mathrm n}\partial_b\phi_{\mathrm n} +\mu^2\phi_{\mathrm n}^2\right)\,d^4x.$$
The total action is defined by this integral when its density is integrable;
it need not converge for an arbitrary smooth global field. For a real
$h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4)$ and $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, the normalized
action difference under $\phi_{\mathrm n}\mapsto\phi_{\mathrm n}+\epsilon h$
is defined by integrating the difference of the displayed densities. That
difference is smooth and supported in $\operatorname{supp}h$, so its integral
is finite even when neither total action exists. Only these compactly
supported variations are used, as in [[post-qft-free-field-model]].
The species, statistics, state, and local action density are physical model inputs. The
present item fixes the exact flat-spacetime free Fock model to which the
later deductions apply.

Use the oriented and time-oriented Minkowski spacetime, signature
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and
$\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3$ from [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Write
$\Box=-\partial_0^2+\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_j^2$. Choose an inverse-length
parameter $\mu\ge0$. When $\mu>0$, the corresponding SI rest mass is
$m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}=\hbar\mu/c>0$; $\mu=0$ denotes the massless branch and
assigns no positive rest mass. For $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, put
$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$, with units
$\mathrm m^{-1}$.

Let $H_\mu^+$, $d\nu_\mu$, $H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C)$, and
$K_\mu:\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)\to H_\mu$ be the future mass shell, measure,
one-particle Hilbert space, and Fourier restriction of
[[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. In the massless case the null apex is omitted;
it has measure zero. The shell measure is
$d\nu_\mu=d^3\mathbf k/((2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k))$.

Use the symmetric bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(H_\mu)$, vacuum
$\Omega=(1,0,0,\ldots)$, and dense finite-particle domain
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ from
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The Fock pairing is linear in its second
variable. Creation $a^\dagger(h)$ is linear in $h$, while annihilation $a(h)$
is conjugate-linear in $h$. For $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ define the
complex-linear smeared scalar field on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ by

$$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f).$$

For real $f$, this is the symmetric scalar field whose self-adjoint closure
and bounded Weyl functions are constructed in
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. A smeared field is a domain-qualified
operator-valued distribution; the item introduces no pointwise operator
$\Phi_\mu(x)$.

Define $d\Gamma_s(\omega_\mu)$ on the $n$-particle sector as multiplication
by $\sum_{r=1}^n\omega_\mu(\mathbf k_r)$, with value zero on the vacuum
sector. The exact maximal domain is

$$D(d\Gamma_s(\omega_\mu))= \left\{\Psi:\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{(H_\mu^+)^n} \left|\sum_{r=1}^n\omega_\mu(\mathbf k_r)\right|^2 |\Psi_n(\mathbf k_1,\ldots,\mathbf k_n)|^2\,d\nu_\mu^n<\infty\right\}.$$

The physical Hamiltonian of this selected model is the vacuum-subtracted
self-adjoint operator
$H_\mu^{\mathrm{phys}}=\hbar c\,d\Gamma_s(\omega_\mu)$ on that domain, as
defined by the multiplier construction of
[[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]]. It has units of joules and
$H_\mu^{\mathrm{phys}}\Omega=0$. No infinite zero-point-energy sum is part of
this definition. The canonical scalar engineering dimension is
$\mathrm m^{-1}$; a spacetime test function of unit $\mathrm m^{-3}$ makes the
smeared field dimensionless, consistently with
[[def-qft-framework-units]].

items.title: Scalar distribution, covariance, locality and spectrum
items.design_state: Complete conditional deductions for the real scalar model: Klein-Gordon equation, covariance, forward spectrum, exact mass gap, and local Weyl commutativity.
items.physical_scope: Conditional properties of the selected four-dimensional real scalar free Fock model: the smeared Klein–Gordon field, proper orthochronous Poincare covariance, vacuum and forward-cone spectrum, exact mass gap, and isotony and spacelike commutativity of bounded local Weyl algebras.
items.statement:
Assume the scalar model adoption planned in
[[post-qft-free-field-model]] and Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]]. Let $\mu\ge0$ and use the model, shell, field,
vacuum, and units of [[def-qft-free-scalar-model]] and
[[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. These are conditional model deductions, with no
empirical premise.

For every Schwartz test $f$, $\Phi_\mu(f)$ is defined on
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$; for real $f$ it is symmetric and essentially
self-adjoint there. Distributionally,
$\Phi_\mu((\Box-\mu^2)f)=0$. The Fock lift of the proper orthochronous
Poincare action is unitary, leaves $\Omega$ invariant, and implements
covariance of the smeared field. For real Schwartz tests the vacuum
two-point form is $\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(f)\Phi_\mu(g)\Omega\rangle=\langle K_\mu f,K_\mu g\rangle_2$, and it is nonnegative when $g=f$. The
joint spectrum of spacetime translations is contained in the closed forward
cone.

For real compactly supported smooth tests with pairwise spacelike-separated
supports, the smeared fields commute on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fin}}$. The
bounded local Weyl algebras are isotonic and algebras for spacelike-separated
regions commute. The physical Hamiltonian is self-adjoint on the exact
multiplier domain in [[def-qft-free-scalar-model]], is nonnegative, and has
zero-energy eigenspace $\ker H_\mu^{\mathrm{phys}}=\mathbb C\Omega$.
Thus its normalized zero-energy vectors are $e^{i\theta}\Omega$ for
$\theta\in\mathbb R$. If $\mu>0$, the infimum of its
positive spectrum is $\hbar c\mu=m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}c^2$. If $\mu=0$, its
positive spectrum has no gap above zero.

items.title: Gaussian free vacuum and time-ordered carrier
items.design_state: Complete conditional vacuum Wick recursion, Gaussian Weyl expectation and exact distributional time-ordered two-point carrier; no interacting convergence or local-product claim.
items.physical_scope: Conditional vacuum, smeared-field moments, bounded Weyl expectations and the exact distributional time-ordered two-point carrier for the selected real scalar free Fock model. No interacting convergence or renormalized local product is claimed.
items.statement:
Assume the scalar model adoption planned in
[[post-qft-free-field-model]], Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]], and the exact model of
[[def-qft-free-scalar-model]]. For real Schwartz tests $f_1,\ldots,f_n$,
the vacuum expectation of the ordered product of smeared fields is zero
when $n$ is odd. When $n$ is even, it is the sum over pairings of products
of the corresponding two-point functions
$\langle K_\mu f_r,K_\mu f_s\rangle_2$ for $r<s$ in each pair. For a real
Schwartz test $f$, the bounded Weyl operator has vacuum expectation
$\langle\Omega,W_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle
=\exp(-\|K_\mu f\|_2^2/2)$.

The time-ordered two-point carrier is the tempered distribution $H_\mu$
defined by the partial spatial Fourier formula of
[[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]]. It agrees with the ordered Wightman
distributions away from equal-time coincidence and satisfies
$(\Box-\mu^2)H_\mu=i\delta_0$. The formula fixes its extension at coincidence
and includes no additional prefactor $i$. These are conditional deductions
for the selected free model.

title: Exact real scalar free model — Examples

items.title: Spacelike vacuum correlation without field commutator
items.design_state: Complete massless conditional example with compact spacelike-separated tests, explicit regulated Wightman kernel limit, and commuting local Weyl operators.
items.physical_scope: A conditional calculation in the massless branch of the selected real scalar free model using compactly supported spacetime tests in strictly spacelike-separated regions. It reports no experiment or signaling result.
items.statement:
In the massless branch $\mu=0$, there are nonnegative real spacetime tests
$f,g$ of unit $\mathrm m^{-3}$ with strictly spacelike-separated supports
for which the vacuum
two-point function $\langle\Omega,\Phi_0(f)\Phi_0(g)\Omega\rangle$ is
strictly positive, while the smeared field commutator and the commutator of
the corresponding bounded local Weyl operators vanish. This is a state
correlation in the selected model; it is not a measurement report or a
signaling claim.
